input_box_content.user_input_content:
=== CHARACTER LOCK — STRICT ===

YOUNG RIVEN:

Use the provided Young Riven reference image as the strict primary character reference.

Preserve Young Riven's exact facial identity, facial structure, pale-blonde hair, hairstyle, eye color, child body proportions, clothing, boots, and overall silhouette.

Young Riven must remain unmistakably the same child throughout the entire video.

She is a young village girl with a naturally curious, energetic, stubborn, and independent personality.

She has no formal sword training.

She has never properly handled this weapon before.

Her interaction with the sword must therefore feel exploratory and inexperienced.

She does not know the correct grip.

She does not know the correct stance.

She underestimates the weight of the weapon.

Her movements must remain physically believable for a young child handling an adult weapon.

Do not make her fight like an experienced warrior.

Do not give her professional sword techniques.

Do not make her acrobatic.

Do not make her unnaturally strong.

Do not make her performance theatrical or exaggerated.

Young Riven remains completely silent throughout this video.


RIVEN'S FATHER:

Use the provided Father reference image as the strict primary character reference.

Preserve his exact facial identity, facial structure, hair, beard, body proportions, clothing, and overall silhouette.

He is a former warrior now living a quiet rural life.

His movements are calm, economical, and physically controlled.

During the beginning of the video, he remains outside near the chopping area.

The sound of his axe striking wood can occasionally be heard from inside the cottage.

Later, he notices Young Riven practicing with his sword.

He does not become angry.

He does not immediately confront her.

He does not speak.

He simply stops and watches.

His reaction should be restrained and natural.

The Father remains completely silent throughout this video.


=== WEAPON LOCK — STRICT ===

Use the provided Old Sword reference image as the strict weapon reference.

Preserve the sword's blade shape, proportions, crossguard, worn leather grip, pommel, materials, and weathered condition.

This is an old adult sword that belongs to Riven's father.

It is a real physical weapon.

It has realistic weight and inertia.

The sword is noticeably too large and too heavy for Young Riven, but not comically oversized.

She can lift it using both hands, but the effort must be physically visible.

The sword's weight must influence her arms, shoulders, posture, balance, and momentum.

Do not allow the weapon to change length, shape, or design between shots.

No magic.

No glow.

No energy.

No supernatural effects.


=== ENVIRONMENT LOCK — STRICT ===

Use the provided Riven Village / Home reference image as the strict environment reference.

Preserve the recognizable family cottage, interior architecture, doorway, yard, nearby old tree, chopping block, stacked firewood, vegetation, and small dirt-and-grass area beside the house.

Maintain believable spatial continuity between the cottage interior, doorway, exterior yard, chopping area, and open ground beside the cottage.

The village remains peaceful.

Soft natural morning sunlight.

Gentle mountain wind.

Subtle distant birds and village ambience.

Inside the cottage, the atmosphere is quiet and slightly darker than outside.

The father's old sword is resting against the wooden wall when the video begins.


=== TECHNICAL ===

High-end live-action cinematic realistic dark fantasy.

Cinematic widescreen composition.

Feature-film quality.

Grounded medieval fantasy.

Realistic human anatomy.

Realistic child anatomy and proportions.

Natural human movement.

Grounded physical interaction.

Realistic sword weight and metal physics.

Realistic balance and momentum.

Realistic cloth and hair physics.

Maintain strict facial identity, costume consistency, sword consistency, body proportions, and environment continuity throughout the whole video.

Use patient cinematic camera movement.

Allow actions to develop clearly.

Do not rush the beginning.

The first physical contact between Young Riven and the sword is an important character moment.

Avoid excessive cuts.

Avoid rapid montage.

Avoid unnecessary background activity.

Avoid exaggerated comedy.

Avoid exaggerated facial expressions.

Avoid professional martial arts movement.

Avoid supernatural movement.

Avoid flashy effects.

No spoken dialogue anywhere in this video.

No background conversations.

No intelligible human speech.

No subtitles.

No captions.

No visible text.

No watermark.

No logo.

Audio:

quiet cottage ambience,
gentle morning wind outside,
distant birds,
soft cloth movement,
wooden floor creaks,
realistic metal movement,
Young Riven's natural breathing,
subtle physical effort sounds.

From outside the cottage, occasionally hear the clear distant sound of the Father's axe striking wood.

The axe sound should establish that her father is still outside working.

No background music.


=== GLOBAL ACTION ===

Open directly on a close cinematic view of the worn leather grip and crossguard of the old sword resting against the cottage wall.

Young Riven is already standing close to the weapon, just outside the frame.

Her hand slowly enters the composition and moves toward the sword grip.

She almost touches it.

Then she hesitates.

From outside:

THOCK.

The sound of her father's axe striking wood.

Riven stops.

She looks toward the open doorway.

Another distant axe strike confirms that her father is still outside working.

Riven looks back toward the sword.

Her curiosity wins.

She slowly places her hand around the worn leather grip.

This is the first time she physically touches the weapon.

She initially tries to move it too casually and immediately discovers that it is much heavier than she expected.

She brings in her second hand and carefully gains control of it.

Riven quietly carries the sword outside.

She moves into the small open dirt-and-grass area beside the cottage.

She tries to imitate what she imagines a warrior should look like.

She attempts one inexperienced sword swing.

The weight and momentum of the weapon pull her off balance.

Riven falls naturally onto the dirt and grass.

The sword lands safely beside her.

She sits there for a moment.

She looks at the sword.

Instead of leaving it, she reaches for it again.

Riven stands back up and takes the sword with both hands.

Without realizing it, her father has stopped working.

He quietly watches her from near the cottage.

Riven does not notice him.

End with Riven standing again with the sword while her father silently observes her.


=== SCENES ===

Shot 1 — THE FIRST TOUCH

Extreme cinematic close-up of the old sword.

Frame primarily the worn leather grip, simple crossguard, and a small section of the weathered blade.

The sword remains resting against the wooden wall.

The cottage is quiet.

Young Riven's hand slowly enters the frame.

Her fingers move toward the leather grip.

Do not rush the movement.

Her fingertips come very close.

Then stop.

THOCK.

A distant axe strike is heard outside.

Riven's hand remains suspended near the sword.

CUT.


Shot 2 — IS HE STILL OUTSIDE?

Medium close-up on Young Riven.

Her eyes move away from the sword toward the open cottage doorway.

Through the doorway, bright morning light enters the darker room.

Do not clearly reposition her father into the interior.

He remains outside.

Another distant sound:

THOCK.

Riven listens.

She understands that her father is still occupied outside.

Her eyes slowly return toward the sword.

Hold briefly on her expression.

Curiosity overcomes hesitation.

Cut back toward the sword.

Riven's hand reaches forward again.

Her fingers finally touch the worn leather grip.

They slowly close around it.

Keep this moment quiet and physical.

No magical reaction.

No dramatic sound effect.

It is simply a child touching her father's old weapon for the first time.

Riven tries to pull the sword toward herself with one hand.

It barely moves.

Her expression changes subtly.

She expected it to be easier.

She tries again.

The sword shifts unexpectedly under its weight.

Riven quickly brings her second hand onto the grip and steadies it before it falls.

A small realistic metallic scrape against the floor.

Riven freezes briefly.

She looks toward the doorway again.

The father does not enter.

Riven carefully lifts the sword using both hands.

Visible effort in her arms, shoulders, and posture.

CUT.


Shot 3 — OUTSIDE

Follow Young Riven from behind and slightly beside her as she carefully carries the sword through the cottage doorway.

Do not make her move quickly.

The sword is awkward for her.

Its weight is visible in her posture.

She occasionally adjusts both hands to maintain control.

Riven moves away from the doorway and enters the small dirt-and-grass area beside the cottage.

The environment opens around her.

Soft morning sunlight.

Gentle wind.

Quiet village ambience.

Riven stops.

She looks around briefly.

She believes she is alone.

She turns her attention back toward the sword.

She plants her feet.

She tries to imitate what she imagines a real warrior should look like.

Her posture is serious but inexperienced.

Her feet are not positioned correctly.

Her grip is imperfect.

She looks down briefly and adjusts herself based entirely on instinct.

Then she prepares to swing.

CUT.


Shot 4 — THE FIRST SWING

Medium-wide side composition.

Keep Young Riven's entire body and the complete sword clearly readable.

Riven raises the heavy sword with both hands.

The effort is obvious.

She takes a natural breath.

Then she attempts a strong diagonal swing.

At first, she appears confident.

The blade begins moving.

Its physical weight creates more momentum than Riven expected.

The sword pulls her upper body forward.

Her balance immediately becomes unstable.

Her feet scramble across the dirt as she tries to recover.

She cannot stop the momentum.

Riven loses her balance and falls naturally onto the grass and dirt.

The sword lands safely beside her.

No injury.

No blade contact with her body.

No exaggerated slapstick.

No dramatic reaction.

The environment becomes quiet again.

Hold on Riven sitting on the ground.

She looks slightly embarrassed and frustrated.

CUT.


Shot 5 — SHE GETS BACK UP

Medium intimate composition.

Young Riven remains sitting on the ground.

Her pale-blonde hair is slightly messier.

A little dirt now marks her clothing.

The old sword lies beside her.

Riven looks at it.

Hold.

She looks toward the cottage briefly.

Then back toward the sword.

She could simply leave it there.

Instead, Riven reaches toward the grip.

Her hand closes around it again.

She uses both hands and begins standing.

Do not make the movement heroic.

The sword is still heavy.

Riven gets fully back onto her feet.

She adjusts her grip.

She adjusts her stance.

She is still inexperienced.

But she is determined to try again.

Riven focuses entirely on the weapon.

She does not look behind herself.

Slowly reveal that her father is now visible near the cottage behind her.

He has stopped chopping wood.

He stands quietly and watches his daughter.

Do not make him angry.

Do not make him smile broadly.

His expression is calm and restrained.

There is subtle curiosity and recognition in the way he watches her.

Riven has no idea that he is there.

Keep Riven clearly in the foreground with her father farther behind her.

Riven tightens both hands around the sword grip.

She prepares herself for another attempt.

Her father remains completely silent.

Hold.

CUT.


=== END STATE FOR CONTINUITY ===

Young Riven is standing in the dirt-and-grass area beside the family cottage.

She holds her father's old sword with both hands.

She has attempted her first swing, lost her balance, and fallen.

She has chosen to pick the sword back up and stand again.

She is preparing to make another attempt.

Her father has stopped working and is now standing quietly near the cottage behind her.

He has seen what she is doing.

Young Riven has not noticed him.

Neither character is speaking.

The father does not approach her.

End with Young Riven focused on the sword in the foreground while her father silently watches from behind.


=== MOOD ===

Quiet.

Curious.

Intimate.

Playful but grounded.

The beginning should feel especially patient.

The important progression is not simply that Young Riven takes the sword.

The audience should experience her decision:

the sword
→ her hand approaches
→ hesitation
→ father's axe outside
→ she checks the doorway
→ looks back at the sword
→ first physical contact.

After she takes the weapon outside, the tone becomes slightly more playful through her inexperienced attempt to imitate a warrior.

Do not turn the fall into comedy.

The important character moment comes afterward.

Riven falls.

She has no audience that she knows of.

Nobody tells her to continue.

She simply looks at the sword, chooses to pick it back up, and stands again.

End quietly with her father discovering this part of her personality without Riven realizing that he is watching.
